historical_references.reference: Ashoka the Great was a Mauryan emperor who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from 268 to 232 BCE. He was the founder of the Mauryan Empire and the most important emperor of his dynasty. Ashoka's inscriptions record his military conquests, as well as details of his Dharma or 'righteous rule' which set new standards for governance in ancient India. He was a champion of Buddhism and initiated the third Buddhist council at Pataliputra.

historical_references.reference: Ashkaa was a legendary queen of the Vedic period, traditionally described as the wife of the god Indra. The Mahabharata mentions Ashkaa as the mother of the Pandava brothers, born when Indra disguised himself as a serpent and entered a sacrifice. Ashkaa is also the name of a constellation, believed to have been named after this queen.
